saints.name: St. Lawrence O'Toole
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The reforming Archbishop of Dublin who shepherded his people through the Norman conquest of Ireland…
biography: Born in 1128 at Kilkea in County Kildare, the son of a Leinster chieftain, Lorcán Ua Tuathail was handed over at the age of ten as a hostage to Dermot MacMurrough and held for two years in harsh custody. Freed through the abbot of Glendalough, he stayed on as a monk, and at twenty-six was himself elected abbot, reforming the abbey on Augustinian lines.

In 1162 he was chosen Archbishop of Dublin, the first Gael to hold that Hiberno-Norse see; he fed the poor daily at his table and lived in hair shirt and fast. When Norman knights stormed Dublin in 1170 while he negotiated outside its walls, he rushed back and stopped the slaughter; thereafter Gael, Norse, and Norman alike sought him as mediator.

Clubbed down by a madman while saying Mass at Becket's tomb in Canterbury, he rose and finished the Mass. He attended the Third Lateran Council in 1179 and was named papal legate. On a last embassy to Henry II he fell ill and died at Eu in Normandy on 14 November 1180; canonized in 1225, he is patron of the Archdiocese of Dublin.
saints.knownFor: Reform of the Church and peacemaking during the Norman invasion.
